## Theorem LP028-F2: different minimal observation sets for endpoints versus shortest BRC

Fix integer `n >= 2` (the native application is `n=6`), an integer `r>=1`, and a declared signed coordinate shell

`S_r^n={d in Z^n : G(d)=sum_i d_i²=r²}`.

Choose a subset `I` of the `n` native positive unit-axis updates `U_i(d)=d+e_i`. The **known initial squared norm** is `r²`; the future observation signature consists only of the exact post-update squared norms

`Q_I(d)=(G(U_i(d)))_{i in I}`.

Let `T(d)=sum_i |d_i|` be the unweighted native shortest path length and `B(d)=T(d)! / prod_i |d_i|!` the existing positive integer shortest word/BRC multiplicity.

**(a) Signed-endpoint recovery.** `Q_I` is injective on `S_r^n` **if and only if** `I={1,...,n}`. Its inverse for a full signature is

`d_i=(G(U_i(d))-r²-1)/2`.

For any omitted index `j`, the two distinct valid states `r e_j` and `-r e_j` have identical `Q_I`. Thus the declared basis of unit-axis norm probes requires **all six** for universal full signed X6 recovery, on every positive integer-radius shell.

**(b) Shortest-BRC recovery.** For the joint observer `(T(d),B(d))`, any `n-1` of those same probes are sufficient on **every** `S_r^n`. If only index `j` is omitted, recover all observed coordinates from `Q_I`; the remaining magnitude is the exact integer root

`|d_j|=sqrt(r²-sum_{i in I}d_i²)`.

Hence the full absolute-count tuple, its sum `T`, and multinomial `B` are determined even when the missing coordinate's sign is unknown.

This is also **minimal for a probe set that must work for all positive integer r**. If `|I|<=n-2`, choose two unprobed distinct axes `j,k` and `r=5`. The states `d=5e_j` and `d'=3e_j+4e_k` have equal squared norm 25 and the same constant `Q_I=(26,...,26)`, but `(T(d),B(d))=(5,1)` and `(T(d'),B(d'))=(7,35)`. Even B alone differs. Thus the universal minimum for the shortest-BRC scalar (and length) is exactly `n-1`, whereas for the signed endpoint it is exactly `n` under this declared probe family.

**Proof:** Expand `G(d+e_i)=G(d)+2d_i+1=r²+2d_i+1`. This yields the full inverse and the omitted-coordinate witnesses. For `n-1` probes, the known `r²` determines the missing absolute coordinate by the displayed perfect-square equation, and the BRC formula depends only on absolute counts. The radius-five equal-signature counterexample holds for every proper probe subset missing at least two indices. This proves both minimality claims and all edge cases for `r>=1`. QED.

**Scope:** This compares exact observations on *fixed-radius full signed native displacement states*, not physical measurements, a global origin, a new dynamics, a final nonnegative Cell encoding, or complete ordered-path provenance. Full signed endpoint recovery suffices for subsequent deterministic endpoint operations; arbitrary ordered-path observables still require path labels. Single-probe completeness depends on the selected future-operation and observer language, not just on current norm.
